info.title: Junctura Capability Extensions v1
info.description: Implemented: Application Authority, C1 Registry, C2 direct Trust/discovery and trust graph, protected Audit, opt-in C4A single invocation and opt-in C4B bounded composition. C3 is an offline resolver used by composition validation. C4B remains disabled by default; no delegation, cancellation, resume, automatic retry, HA or general side effects. Operation-level status identifies implemented subsets.

get.summary: Discover only exact published versions with an active discover grant
get.description: Implemented C1 Registry lifecycle. C1 provider-owner/capabilities.publish visibility is retained. Consumer GET/list requires a current exact discover grant, verified active backend binding, the complete required permission set and live provider/consumer/approval authority. Hidden versions/drafts/approval metadata are concealed. Additionally, published versions exposed through the catalog visibility level are returned to every authorized tenant caller (tenant), to callers whose token groups name a designated unit (units) or whose caller application is designated (applications); exposure never crosses tenants. No invocation is performed. See CAPABILITY_DIRECT_TRUST.md and CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.md.

put.summary: Set how widely a published version is exposed in the tenant catalog
put.description: Implemented catalog visibility. The level is tenant (whole organization), units (only the named units, matched against the caller's token groups), applications (only the named caller applications) or hidden (default: only exact grant discovery and management views). Changing the level requires capabilities.publish, or capabilities.write plus ownership of the provider application, an exact If-Match, existing confirmed units and same-tenant applications in the designation list. Tenant and hidden levels clear both designation lists. The change is audited as capability.visibility_changed. See CAPABILITIES.md.

get.summary: Read the tenant trust graph
get.description: Implemented. Read-only view of direct cross-application trust: applications as nodes and grants as edges, with the effective state (pending, active, expired, revoked) and expiry. An administrator with trust.approve or a read-only viewer with audit.read sees every grant of its tenant; a writer with trust.write sees only grants whose provider application it owns. readOnly is true when the caller holds neither trust.write nor trust.approve. No query parameters: the tenant and scope come from the verified caller. At most 500 newest edges are returned; truncated reports more. See CAPABILITY_DIRECT_TRUST.md.

post.summary: Accept one guarded pinned capability execution
post.description: Opt-in guarded execution. C4B accepts only target and input and pins a published caller-owned composition. Every step rechecks original OIDC authority, active apps and independent same-tenant direct invoke grants; providers authenticate and redeem single-use step-bound tickets. C4B replay returns the durable reservation and never restores a lost lease or retries ambiguous work. Results require original consumer/subject/client and current authority. Success requires validated final output and confirmed Flowable history. No cancellation, resume, delegation or automatic retries. C4A retains its documented untouched-work replay contract. See CAPABILITY_COMPOSITION.md and CAPABILITY_EXECUTION.md. An optional context with purpose, dataSubject and dataSubjectKind declares why the call is made and whose data it concerns; it is bound into the idempotent request, sealed into the audit chain, passed to the provider on ticket redemption and listed for the data subject by GET /v1/me/data-access. When the context names a dataSubject, an active consent of that person for the consumer application, capability and purpose is required (403 consent_required, consent_revoked or consent_expired), unless emergency is true with a justification; emergency calls are queued for review and at most five may be pending per consumer (429 emergency_review_backlog).

get.summary: Query authorized audit events
get.description: app=self selects only events of the verified app. Otherwise a caller with the verified regulator role sees application events for assigned units, with actor, subjectId, resourceRef, purpose and meta withheld for restricted events. A management principal with audit.read can see tenant platform audit items and the structural projection of app events. subjectId filtering is unavailable in the management view. Unit and actor context come from verified identity. Results are ordered by occurredAt and eventId descending. Keep scope and filters unchanged with nextCursor. Existing management clients may use since and until and keep the same platform item fields. The action filter matches the event field on platform items.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Scope to the verified calling app. Required for the app view. Mutually exclusive with unit.

parameters.name: subjectId
parameters.description: Available to the app and the authorized regulator within their scopes.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Regulator filter for an assigned unit.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower timestamp.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper timestamp.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Legacy alias for from. Supply at most one.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Legacy alias for to. Supply at most one.

post.description: An active registered app sends only the declared event fields. Core resolves the actor from the app credential or a verified delegated user context bound to the app, stamps the app, unit when verified, and time, and appends to the tenant hash chain. subjectId is supplied only when the event concerns that subject. Use opaque references, coded purpose and non-sensitive meta. An identical retry replays the original 201 receipt. A changed request with the same key returns 422 idempotency_key_reused. Up to 120 new entries per app per minute.

get.summary: Export an authorized audit view
get.description: app=self selects only events of the verified app. Otherwise a caller with the verified regulator role sees application events for assigned units, with actor, subjectId, resourceRef, purpose and meta withheld for restricted events. A management principal with audit.read can see tenant platform audit items and the structural projection of app events. subjectId filtering is unavailable in the management view. Unit and actor context come from verified identity. Export a consistent snapshot up to the tenant chain head. Each tenant can open two snapshots at a time. An export matching more than 10,000 events fails with 400 audit_export_too_large; narrow the time range and retry. The first line identifies the head even for an empty result. An empty tenant chain has sequence 0 and the zero hash of 64 zeros, which the chain verifier also accepts as the genesis predecessor. Event lines carry their chain sequence and stored digest for reconciliation. Scoped exports can have gaps and redacted fields; verify the full tenant chain through the existing privileged verify endpoint.

parameters.name: app
parameters.description: Scope to the verified calling app. Required for the app view. Mutually exclusive with unit.

parameters.name: subjectId
parameters.description: Available to the app and the authorized regulator within their scopes.

parameters.name: unit

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower timestamp.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper timestamp.

200.description: The first line is AuditExportHead; subsequent lines are authorized events in increasing chain sequence.

schema.description: UTF-8 JSON lines. Each line follows the schema AuditExportLine unless otherwise specified.

post.summary: Seal pending audit events and verify the tenant hash chain
post.description: Implemented. Seals the caller tenant's pending audit events into a SHA-256 hash chain, then recomputes every sealed entry. A modified, deleted or reordered sealed event, or a removed newest entry, is reported in firstBreak; nothing is sealed on top of a broken chain. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. The database administrator remains trusted; see AUDIT.md.

200.description: Verification result; verified=false is a successful check that found tampering.

get.summary: List the caller tenant's enrolled management principals
get.description: Implemented. Returns up to 1000 enrolled principals of the caller's tenant and issuer with subject, issuer, managementClient, permissions, enabled, and the optional presentation profile displayName, organization, jobTitle and kind (admin or application), each null when unset. Never returns secrets, tokens or request bodies and never calls the identity provider's admin API. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function enforces the tenant, issuer and permission. No query parameters.

200.description: Enrolled principals of the caller tenant

get.summary: Read the tenant/application tree with current trust relations
get.description: Implemented. Builds a read-only tree from real data: the root is the caller tenant (kind platform), children are the applications registered in that tenant (kind application), and relations are non-revoked, unexpired direct trust grants between those applications. Relation labels are the real published capability title, falling back to the exact capabilityId. There is no separate organization table, so applications appear directly under the tenant. At most 1000 applications and 500 relations; truncated reports more. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. No query parameters.

get.summary: Read one-minute traffic buckets for the recent window
get.description: Implemented. Returns exactly minutes chronological one-minute buckets ending with the current minute, including empty minutes as zeroes, with requests, 4xx/5xx errors, average latency and maximum latency, plus totals for the window. Counters are real observations recorded as responses finish. They live in the Core process only, are per instance and reset when Core restarts; no database or persistence is involved. Metrics requests are counted like any other request. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

parameters.name: minutes
parameters.description: Number of one-minute buckets ending with the current minute.

200.description: Traffic series for the requested window

get.summary: Read the newest requests observed by Core
get.description: Implemented. Returns up to limit of the newest requests, newest first. Each entry contains only the observation time, method, normalized path, status and duration. Query strings, fragments, headers, bodies, tokens, subjects and recognizable UUID/token path segments are never retained. The in-memory ring holds at most the newest 200 requests; it is per Core process and resets when Core restarts. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of newest requests to return.

get.summary: List the data subject's visible access events
get.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Merge capability calls and application events declared visible to this data subject at append time. Order by accessedAt descending and accessId descending. Use accessId for flagging either source. Preserve entries, generatedAt and truncated; truncated is true when nextCursor is present.

post.summary: Flag an access event for review
post.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Applies to either visible source. Store a separate report. Retrying the same reason returns the original report; attempting to change it returns 409. Nonvisible entries return 404.

get.summary: List the data subject's consents
get.description: Return the latest 200 consents belonging to the data subject. Uses the authenticated login, tenant and issuer for compatibility. A supplied subjectId claim must match the operator binding or the request returns 403.

post.summary: Grant consent as the data subject
post.description: Grant the declared purposes for an existing capability, expiring within 366 days. Provide either consumerAppId for an active app or recipientUnit for a confirmed unit in the same tenant. A unit grant requires an operator-bound subjectId from the subject login. App grants keep their existing scope.

Revoking an already revoked consent returns its current representation. Uses the authenticated login, tenant and issuer for compatibility. A supplied subjectId claim must match the operator binding or the request returns 403.

post.summary: Submit feedback on the subject's own break-glass access
post.description: Use the verified token subjectId, tenant and issuer; a supplied subject identifier never selects another person. A missing verified claim returns 403. Use the execution ID from the break-glass access entry. Feedback is separate from the management review and the original audit event. Identical retries return the saved receipt; different feedback after submission conflicts. Keep personal content out of message.

get.description: Implemented. Break-glass calls in the caller's tenant with justification and review state. Requires trust.approve.

get.summary: Read aggregate record and file counts for the caller tenant
get.description: Implemented. Returns per-application structured record counts by collection plus aggregate file count, bytes, quarantine count and last modification time, and tenant totals. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the database function and private role enforce tenant scope. Record content, object keys, file names and bytes are never returned. Object metadata is reduced from the object filer; if the filer is not configured files is null for every application, and if it is configured but unavailable the request fails closed. No query parameters.

get.summary: Browse one directory level of an application's object store
get.description: Implemented. Returns exactly one level of the application's private file tree: folders with aggregate file count, bytes and latest modification time, and files with a partially masked name, extension, size, scan status and modification time. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the storage summary function and private role enforce the permission. The path defaults to the root, is canonicalised, rejects traversal, control characters and segments longer than 255 characters, and is limited to 512 characters. Object keys, internal filer paths, versions and bytes are never returned. The object filer must be configured; if it is unavailable the request fails closed.

parameters.name: application

get.summary: Read the inferred field structure of an application's collections
get.description: Implemented. Returns each collection owned by the application with its record count, latest update time and the field names inferred from at most the 200 newest records. Field types are string, number, boolean, object, array, mixed or null; fillRate is the percentage of sampled records where the field is present and not null. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the new migration-026 function and private role enforce permission and tenant scope. Record values, sample rows, object keys and bytes are never returned.

parameters.name: application
parameters.description: Application whose collection structure is read.

get.summary: List the caller tenant workflow executions, newest first
get.description: Implemented. Returns a bounded page of Flowable history scoped to the caller tenant. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant; the private workflow audit role enforces the permission. Running rows include the active task name, assignee and candidate groups. The title is the workflow definition name, followed by input.reference only when that value is a string matching ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]{0,31}$; without a definition name it is null. No other input fields contribute; personal names, other identifiers, record content and workflow variables are never included. The internal junctura_c4a_single definition is excluded.

200.description: Workflow executions of the caller tenant

get.summary: Read per-feature call counts for the recent window
get.description: Implemented. Groups the same real, in-memory one-minute observations as getTrafficMetrics by product feature (data, files, workflows, approvals, sharing, capabilities, applications, consents, secrets, audit, other), derived from the normalized request path. Each feature carries requests, 4xx/5xx errors, average and maximum latency and a per-minute request series, sorted by requests descending. Counters live in the Core process only, are per instance and reset when Core restarts. A verified management principal with audit.read is required. Query parameters are closed; unknown, repeated or malformed values return 400.

parameters.name: minutes
parameters.description: Number of one-minute buckets ending with the current minute.

200.description: Per-feature traffic for the requested window

get.summary: Read the read-only workflow dashboard for the caller tenant
get.description: Implemented. Returns every business workflow definition with its owning product, ordered steps with responsible parties, and counts of running, completed and cancelled executions, plus totals. It is a read-only aggregate: it never starts, completes or cancels anything and never reads workflow variables or personal data. Technical definitions used only for Core verification are excluded. Requires a verified management principal with audit.read in its own tenant. The query string must be empty.

200.description: Workflow dashboard for the caller tenant
